newsitem.title: GERMANY: SKW Trostberg drops after bank downgrade.
newsitem.headline: SKW Trostberg drops after bank downgrade.

text.p: Shares in German speciality chemical group SKW Trostberg dropped nearly nine percent on Friday after its nine-month results disappointed analysts and prompted some of them to lower earnings forecasts.
SKW shares touched a daily low of 41 marks before recovering slightly to trade down 2.12 marks 42.80 marks, or a loss of 4.7 percent.
The broader German market was at new record high levels, with the DAX index of 30 leading shares up 26.16 points at 2,739.38 points, a gain of nearly one percent.
SKW initially fell after the firm said nine-month sales rose four percent to 2.97 billion marks over year-ago levels.
But heavy selling emerged after BHF Bank cut its recommendations on SKW to "hold" from "buy" and reduced its earnings per share (EPS) estimates.

BHF analyst Ronald Koehler said he cut the group's 1996 EPS to 2.25 marks from 2.65 marks, cut the 1997 EPS to 2.90 marks from 3.10 marks and reduced the 1998 EPS estimate to 3.70 marks from 3.90 marks.
Koehler said the results were slightly disappointing, partly due to ongoing weakness in the construction sector.
